jobs.description: CONTENTS StarkEx Spot Trading and StarkEx Perpetual trading Introduction StarkEx leverages STARK technology to power scalable, self-custodial trading and payment transactions for applications such as DeFi and gaming. StarkEx enables an application to scale significantly and improve transaction speed while also reducing transaction costs. Implementation requires minimal change to existing setups. StarkEx currently supports ETH, synthetic assets, and the following tokens: ERC-20 ERC-721 ERC-1155 StarkEx can also support tokens on other EVM-compatible blockchains. StarkEx is a mature platform that has been deployed on Ethereum Mainnet since June 2020. Before its Mainnet deployment, over 50 million StarkEx transactions were settled on both public and private Ethereum testnets. Many applications currently use StarkEx, including: Client Launch Date Current StarkEx Version rhino.fi (Previously DeversiFi) June 2020 Spot Trading V4 ImmutableX Apr 2021 Spot Trading V3 dYdX Apr 2021 Perpetual trading V1 Sorare June 2021 Spot Trading V4.5 Myria August 2022 Spot Trading V4.5 ApeX pro September 2022 Perpetual trading V2 Reddio October 2022 Spot Trading V4.5 tanX (Previously Brine) June 2023 Spot Trading V4.5 For addresses of deployed StarkEx smart contracts, see Customers and their deployment contract addresses. jobs.title: Playground
jobs.description: CONTENTS A real StarkEx instance compared with the Playground Try StarkEx: Deposit, Withdraw, Settle, and Mint Prerequisites Preparing the Playground Running the Playground So, what happened here? Which transactions did I submit? How do I see the onchain state update? How can I read the offchain vault balances? This is so cool! How do I submit some of my own transactions? I need some more guidance, can you help me? StarkEx Spot Trading Playground tutorial The StarkEx Spot Playground is a deployment of StarkEx for Spot Trading 5.0 on the Goerli testnet that provides a simple demonstration of the StarkEx scalability solution. You can use the Playground to: easily submit transactions to StarkEx, see these transactions in a StarkEx batch, and watch how the state, including your transactions, is updated onchain in the StarkEx contract. If you want to skip a few steps and develop your own application, see the StarkEx SDK and the StarkEx Crypto SDK. If you have questions, at any step of the way, please contact us at info@starkware.co. A real StarkEx instance compared with the Playground Elements of a real StarkEx instance differ from the playground, as described in Table 1, “A real StarkEx instance compared with the Playground”. The purpose of this Playground is to facilitate manual experimentation, but it is not optimized for, nor is it intended to be used for, automated testing. When you are ready to conduct testing, including automation, contact us at info@starkware.co to set up your own dedicated test instance. Table 1. A real StarkEx instance compared with the Playground A real StarkEx instance StarkEx Playground You are the only operator. You have full control of your StarkEx instance. There are multiple operators. You manage the allocation of vault ids as part of your application. The vault id that you choose for your transaction might already be occupied by someone else. You are the only one sending transactions, so you shouldn’t call get_first_unused_tx_id. StarkEx processes transactions sequentially, based on the value of each transaction’s ID, so the ids in your list of transactions must include all integers in the range of values. For example, for a list of three transactions, the list of transaction ID values cannot be 0,1,3, it must be 0,1,2. The list can also be non-sequential, such as 0,2,1. If the list doesn’t include an integer, StarkEx stops processing when it reaches the missing ID and waits for it to be submitted. In order to get the next transaction ID, you must query the StarkEx gateway by calling get_first_unused_tx_id, because other Playground users need to sync the next tx_id. Be aware that StarkEx does not process two transactions with the same ID and does not process a transaction if the transaction with the previous ID has not been processed. The time for a transaction to appear onchain after being submitted can be up to 18 hours. The time for a transaction to appear onchain after being submitted is approximately five minutes. Try StarkEx: Deposit, Withdraw, Settle, and Mint The StarkEx Playground package provides a list of valid, pre-prepared StarkEx transactions, such as deposits, withdrawals, settlements, and mint requests. You also get a Player script that submits these transactions to StarkEx. Simply run the Player and: observe the transactions as they propagate through StarkEx, query StarkEx to see the latest offchain batch with your transactions in it, and watch as a new onchain state is formed in the StarkEx smart contract. For more information about StarkEx, see the High level overview. Prerequisites Git. An Infura endpoint link for the Goerli testnet. If you don’t have one, please open an Ethereum account at https://infura.io/ to acquire a link. Docker. To install Docker on Ubuntu Linux or other Debian-based Linux distributions, enter the following command: $ sudo apt install -y docker.io A Goerli Eth account with enough Eth to pay for the deposit transaction gas. For your convenience, you can try this faucet. Preparing the Playground Procedure Clone the Git repo at https://github.com/starkware-libs/starkex-playground: $ git clone git@github.com:starkware-libs/starkex-playground.git Change to starkex-playground directory: $ cd starkex-playground Build the Docker image: $ docker build -t . --no-cache The Playground package includes the following files: txs.json A list of onchain transactions, including deposits, settlements, and withdrawals that are executed from the Vault range that you were assigned. These transactions are valid and signed by pre-defined users with their public Stark key. This allows you to observe a full StarkEx operation cycle without getting into the details of the exact transaction for each operation. player.py A python script that checks and submits the list of transactions specified in txs.json to the StarkEx contract and the StarkEx offchain service. These transactions are then submitted to the onchain StarkEx service, executed, and added to the batch to be submitted as a new onchain state. Running the Playground Procedure If necessary, change to the starkex-playground directory. Run the Docker image: $ docker run -it root@f4725d0858d2:/app# In the Docker container, you can run the following command for further instructions: root@f4725d0858d2:/app# ./player.py --help Run the Player script by running the following command: $ ./player.py --txs txs.json --node_url --funder_private_key --verbose You can export your Goerli private key from MetaMask: select Account Details from the menu next to the account address. select Export Private Key and provide your MetaMask password. This key is required to fund onchain deposits and will only be used locally to sign the transactions. Analyzing the output The output includes two types: Onchain deposit transactions' description of the StarkEx contract with Etherscan links. See Figure 1, “Onchain transactions”. Offchain

jobs.title: Tech Stack
jobs.description: Select any text and click on the icon to listen! ByGSpeech Skip to content Tech Stack Cairo - a Turing-Complete Programming Language In order to prove the validity of a computation in a STARK proof, it must be expressed in algebraic form. Cairo is a CPU architecture, decoupling the business logic, which can now be written in a high-level programming language from the algebraic representation that can be efficiently proven by STARK. This way, developers can focus on writing the desired business logic, without the need to understand and account for translating it to efficient mathematical representations. Cairo is a modern programming language reminiscent of Rust. Cairo makes it easy to develop, test, and maintain contract logic without the need to deep dive into the STARK algebra. StarkWare defines the Cairo-Architecture and implements it both as a native VM, and as a proving-optimized algebraic form. StarkWare develops additional developer tools around the Cairo programming language, such as compilers from higher-level languages, debugger, IDE support, and more. The Cairo toolchain is developed in Rust for great flexibility, performance, developer experience, and readability. Explore Cairo Starknet: A Decentralized ZK-Rollup Starknet is a permissionless decentralized ZK-Rollup operating as an L2 network over Ethereum. StarkNet solves the blockchain scalability problem by enabling significantly higher network throughput, thus also lower cost per transaction while leveraging Ethereum’s security. Developers can write Starknet contracts using the Cairo language and deploy them on the network, and users can send transactions to these contracts (in a similar manner to Ethereum). The two main components running Starknet are the Sequencer (which generates blocks, similar to miners in Bitcoin or validators in Ethereum) and the Full Node (that syncs on the state of the network). Both are built in Rust, to enable both safety and good performance. This optimizes the proving performance of each transaction execution. A Solidity contract deployed on Ethereum connects the Starknet network (L2) to Ethereum (L1). The Starknet transaction execution environment, called Starknet OS (similar to the Ethereum Virtual Machine), is implemented in Cairo. The Starknet Prover is optimized for performance by implementing C++ and some low-level assembly. It runs over micro-services architecture in the cloud. The Verifier is implemented in Solidity, allowing proofs to be verified on the Ethereum blockchain. Explore Starknet StarkEx: Managed Services StarkWare runs separate instances of its L2 appchain (an L2 system providing scale on top of Ethereum) for premium customers. Such services do the heavy lifting of communicating with the Blockchain and the Application smart contract (over Starknet or Ethereum), to apply off-chain logic as required, and expose an application-specific API, allowing the customers to focus on their core competence. The off-chain services are implemented in Python and typically implement a cloud micro-services architecture. Explore StarkEx Stone Prover Stone Prover, a cornerstone of Starknet’s Layer 2 tech stack, is available under the Apache 2.0 license. It is capable of proving the computational integrity of a VM running Cairo. By nature of the STARK algorithm it implements, the verification of proofs is logarithmic in the size of the Cairo statement (program traces) run. This is leveraged by Starknet for scaling Ethereum. By open-sourcing this robust tool, reflecting the spirit of a truly decentralized and permissionless Layer 2 network, StarkWare offers developers this versatile proving engine for them to prove their Cairo programs and help contribute to the development of Starknet’s ecosystem. Since launch, STARK-tech scaling solutions built with this Prover at their basis have compressed and proved $1T in cumulative transaction volume, 500M transactions, and more than 100M NFT mintings. Explore Stone Prover SHARP Representing StarkWare’s complete commitment to scaling Ethereum, SHARP (SHARed Prover) is poised to redefine the benchmarks of scalability solutions in the Layer 2 crypto domain. Built upon the robust foundation of the Stone Prover, SHARP is a powerful system designed to generate STARK proofs for aggregated Cairo programs. It does this by processing vast amounts of batch transactions off-chain and subsequently validates their computations through an on-chain Solidity verifier contract on Ethereum’s Mainnet. The result is enhanced throughput, reduced gas fees, and minimized latency. Explore SHARP S-two Prover S-two, our open-source next-generation STARK prover, implements the ground-breaking Circle STARK protocol to offer a blazing-fast proving experience. S-two is developed under the Apache 2.0 license from day one. The unprecedented performance facilitated by S-two’s efficient implementation of Circle STARKs will benefit both users and developers in the Starknet ecosystem. It will reduce latency until finality and transaction fees. It will also enable client-side proving and usher in new proving use cases. Explore Stwo Prover Stay up to date with our news and coming up events Subscribe to our mailing list Select and listen

ByGSpeech Skip to content STARK 101 STARK 101 is a hands-on tutorial on how to write a STARK prover from scratch (in Python). 1 STATEMENT, LOW DEGREE EXTENSION, AND COMMITMENT 2 POLYNOMIAL CONSTRAINTS 3 FRI COMMITMENT 4 FRI QUERIES Each section has a short explainer video and a Jupyter practice Notebook. To use the Notebook, you can either install it locally via our GitHub repository, or run it online via Binder. The tutorial assumes familiarity with Python and some mathematical background (including finite field arithmetics). STARK 101 was originally a live workshop, held in Tel Aviv in September 2019 as part of StarkWare Sessions. To run the tutorial online via Binder Start Here Part I: Statement, LDE & Commitment Introducing the statement we will be proving and the concepts of Low Degree Extension (LDE) and commitment using Merkle tree. GitHub, Slides, YouTube Part II: Polynomial Constraints Create a set of polynomial constraints, reduce the original statement to a new one, create a composition polynomial and commit on it. GitHub, Slides, YouTube Part III: FRI Commitment Dive into the FRI protocol and use it to prove that a polynomial is close to one of a bounded degree. GitHub, Slides, YouTube Part IV: The Proof We tie it all together to build an end-to-end proof. GitHub, Slides, YouTube Part V: STARK 101 – Finale A recap, and some ideas on what you can do next. jobs.title: Overview
jobs.description: Select any text and click on the icon to listen! ByGSpeech Skip to content STARK STARK is a proof system. It uses cutting-edge cryptography to provide polylogarithmic verification resources and proof size, with minimal and post-quantum-secure assumptions. What Is ZK-STARK? ZK ZERO-KNOWLEDGE S SCALABLE T TRANSPARENT AR K ARGUMENT OF KNOWLEDGE Zero-Knowledge Inputs used by the off-chain prover are not exposed on the blockchain, thus protecting user’s privacy. What is ZK-STARK? ZK-STARKs, invented by StarkWare, enforce the integrity and privacy of computations on blockchains, using novel cryptographic proofs and modern algebra. ZK-STARKs allow blockchains to move computations to a single off-chain STARK prover and then verify the integrity of those computations using an on-chain STARK Verifier. Want to know more about STARK? jobs.title: Vision and Mission
jobs.description: Select any text and click on the icon to listen! ByGSpeech Skip to content StarkWare Vision and Mission The Big Picture Today, most of our technology infrastructure is at the mercy of big-tech companies and nation states, who at the push of a button could choose to use this infrastructure against us. We should all have the freedom to interact online without living in fear of our favored technology misleading, monitoring or censoring us. At StarkWare we are building infrastructure for an online environment where things work differently. We call it the Integrity Web. We envision it as a layer of the internet that puts you back in control and gives you true ownership of all that matters. What Will the Integrity Web Actually Give Us? The Integrity Web will check that companies and governments are keeping the promises they make to us regarding online interactions. It will verify this in a manner that is so watertight that even the companies of governments will be unable to circumvent or disrupt it. Our vision is a world where integrity is publicly demonstrated, and upheld by all. By integrity, we mean everyone doing the right thing, even when no one is watching. We’re not naive – we know human nature won’t get us there. But math and cryptography will. The Integrity Web concept doesn’t rely on people promising they won’t mislead you, censor, or surveil you. Instead, it will actually be impossible for them to do so because of cryptography deployed globally on blockchains. The Integrity Web will be a secure, transparent, and decentralized online environment where trust is built into the system and cannot be bought or compromised. The Mission The World We Want to Create Our aim is to bring about the Integrity Web. It will connect and scale different blockchains, so they can realize their potential and empower people. We want a world where individuals truly own their digital actions, assets, and lives, and the Integrity Web is the way to achieve it. The Unique Tech We're Using to Do It The missing link that has prevented such an initiative is scale. It has proved impossible until now to achieve mass scale with decentralized networks without compromising blockchain values. The ZK-STARK protocol, invented by StarkWare, changes this dynamic. ZK-STARKs scale blockchain with zero compromises (see Math Never Lies: Why We Scale With STARKS for more details). ZK-STARKs will deliver the Integrity Web, and at StarkWare, we are developing and democratizing their use for global-scale real-world blockchain applications. It’s not just that we scale; it’s also how we scale. ZK-STARKs provide a pathway to privacy on the blockchain. And we use them to offer a user experience on the Integrity Web that is as intuitive as using an app on a smartphone. Tangible Steps on Ethereum; More to Do We have used the tech we have built so far to take tangible steps towards the Integrity Web by successfully scaling Ethereum. We are continually innovating to make sure we are scaling Ethereum in the most efficient and user-friendly way possible. The next part of our mission includes scaling Bitcoin. What is more, we will enable the world’s two biggest blockchains to easily “talk to each other” by enabling trustless interoperability between Bitcoin and Ethereum. The Momentum We’re Creating Matters Far Beyond Finance Blockchain has more and more momentum thanks to scaling, and we are convinced this will revolutionize finance – and beyond. It will actually change the power dynamics between individuals and the tech platforms we use daily. Today, to use the tech platforms that make our lives comfortable, we surrender our agency and data and let big tech act on our behalf, custody our assets, and turn us into the product. If we don’t agree, we’re left behind tech-wise. The Integrity Web will offer a new path. And market pressure will send companies rushing to explore it. Ownership will return to us and real alternatives will arise to serve the many who don’t want to surrender their agency to big tech Our Values These values drive our actions and guide our thinking Integrity It’s all about integrity. Integrity is in our math, in the tech we build, and in our conduct. We ensure that StarkWare and its team always uphold this value, even when no one is watching. Broadness We want to see STARK-based technology adopted far and wide, across continents, cultures, and social classes. This is not only good for humanity, it's good for the technology itself. A diverse and inclusive team and ecosystem most effectively protect networks from the domination of any single entity. In other words, the vision of freedom and sovereignty is best served through widespread adoption. Meritocracy Excellence in mathematics and cryptography drives us. At StarkWare, merit outweighs hierarchy, and we partner with teams committed to top-tier research and development. Community Family, friends, and community form the backbone of a successful company, as well as a free society. Generosity StarkWare is a significant player, but we don’t throw our weight around. Instead, we act with respect and generosity towards everyone—collaborators, competitors, or colleagues. This applies internally too, across all levels. We welcome others outside of StarkWare exploring STARKs and learn from critiques, recognizing that success comes from diverse contributions, and always giving credit to others when it is due. A Final Thought We are a unique company: math and cryptography innovators with a passion for fixing finance and society with math. Our head is in the sky – economics, social theory and math – but our boots are in the mud, writing safe and efficient software for developers and end-users. With our smarts, STARKs, teamwork, and our egalitarian ethos, no blockchain is too steep for StarkWare to scale. Select and listen

ByGSpeech Skip to content The StarkWare Delegation Program Come stake with us StarkWare is excited to support Starknet's security and decentralization by delegating STRK to committed, high-quality validators. Delegation In 2025, StarkWare launched a delegation program in order to support greater decentralization and community involvement in its staking protocol. After several rounds focused on expanding the reach of the program and attracting more stakers, the program’s third round shifts its focus from breadth to depth: fewer validators will receive larger delegations, with higher standards of reliability, availability, and long-term partnership expected in return. Track A Designed for StarkWare’s core validators: serious, highly committed operators with respectable staking amounts and a proven operational record. Track A will include several dozen recipients, each entitled to a delegation of at least 15M STRK, and up to 20M STRK for candidates who qualify under more than one eligibility track, or who have maintained significant testnet activity. All Track A participants must demonstrate 99% mainnet liveness over the last three months, and must qualify under at least one of the following: Top staker: One of the top 8 validators by STRK stake (excluding StarkWare and the Starknet Foundation, which are excluded from the stake ranking). Top-tier infrastructure provider: Established infrastructure providers from other chains that maintain a Starknet staking service. Applications should highlight the other chains the entity operates on, any audits held, and involvement in the Starknet community or efforts to attract non-StarkWare delegation. Ecosystem contributor: Builders contributing to Starknet’s success. Any app builder on Starknet whose app paid at least $2,000/month in network fees on average over the last three months is automatically eligible. Other ecosystem members who have made strong contributions to Starknet or its related technology in the last six months may apply for consideration, highlighting their relevant contribution. Track B Designed for dedicated operators and enthusiasts who take their staking role seriously, actively participate in decentralization discussions, and maintain a testnet presence. Track B will include a handful of recipients, each entitled to a delegation of 5M STRK. This track primarily aims to help cover infrastructure costs for committed individuals with a genuine interest in Starknet staking. Participants must demonstrate 99% liveness over the last three months on both mainnet and testnet. Applicants should describe their interest in Starknet staking, what brought them to participate, and the perspective they can bring going forward. How can I get involved? Apply to join StarkWare’s staking program as a validator! Whether you're a seasoned validator or a STRK holder new to validation, the program offers you options to contribute to Starknet’s security and decentralization and earn rewards in the process. Why Validate through the StarkWare Delegation Program? Earn Competitive Rewards: Receive staking rewards for participating in block validation Strengthen Network Security: Play a crucial role in maintaining the integrity and performance of Starknet Apply Now Track A Requirements Qualify as a top staker, top-tier infrastructure provider, or ecosystem contributor (see track details above) Demonstrate 99% liveness over the last three months on mainnet Maintain 99% mainnet and testnet liveness for the duration of the program Maximum commission capped at 15% Active participation in staking conversations and feedback sessions (approximately one hour per month, when requested) 24/7 on-call service once Staking v3 / decentralized validation is live (targeting 2027) Successfully complete mandatory compliance When applying, please clearly state which track you are applying to and why you meet its criteria. Track B Requirements A statement describing your interest in Starknet staking and the perspective you bring Maintain 99.5% livenessDemonstrate 99% liveness over the last three months on both mainnet and testnet Maintain 99% mainnet and testnet liveness for the duration of the program Maximum commission capped at 15% 24/7 on-call service once Staking v3 / decentralized validation is live (targeting 2027) Successfully complete mandatory compliance When applying, please clearly state which track you are applying to and why you meet its criteria. Purpose of the form: Ensure Network Integrity: By verifying validators, we maintain a secure and trustworthy network environment. Comply with Regulations: Adhering to compliance requirements helps us meet global regulatory standards, reducing risks that could affect all participants. Protect Participants: Compliance helps prevent malicious actors from compromising the network, safeguarding your STRK and the ecosystem’s health. Build a Trustworthy Ecosystem Together: By completing the compliance process, you contribute to a more secure network, benefiting all participants. Program terms FAQs Why did StarkWare launch a staking program? How does the StarkWare Delegation Program work and how can I participate? How can I learn more about the StarkWare Delegation Program? If I'm not yet running a validator on Starknet, how can I participate in the StarkWare Delegation Program? Can I participate as a Starknet validator without applying through StarkWare’s Delegation Program? What is the deadline for applying to the StarkWare Delegation Program? How do I complete the form? Do I need to apply to be a validator each registration round? Can I apply to more than one track or eligibility criterion? What happens to delegations from previous rounds? Why is StarkWare changing the program structure? Select and listen

ByGSpeech Skip to content Licenses Our technology is available under a few different sets of terms, some open source, and some source-available. Smart Contracts: StarkWare’s smart contracts on Ethereum are all open source under Apache 2.0. This includes the StarkEx and Cairo Verifier smart contracts. Cairo Programs: StarkWare’s programs written in Cairo, including business logic included in StarkEx deployments, are open source under Apache 2.0. Cairo Compiler Toolchain: The toolchain used for developing Cairo 1.0 programs is open source under Apache 2.0. Stone Prover: The Stone prover is open-sourced under the Apache 2.0 license. Stwo Prover: The Stwo prover is open-sourced under the Apache 2.0 license. StarkEx Cloud Service: The StarkEx Prover cloud service is closed source, and currently operated by StarkWar If you have any questions about our products and how to use them, talk to us: info@starkware.co Licenses. Our technology is available under a few different sets of terms, some open source, and some source-available. Smart Contracts: StarkWare’s smart contracts on Ethereum are all open source under Apache 2.0. This includes the StarkEx and Cairo Verifier smart contracts. Cairo Programs: StarkWare’s programs written in Cairo, including business logic included in StarkEx deployments, are open source under Apache 2.0. Cairo Compiler Toolchain: The toolchain used for developing Cairo 1.0 programs is open source under Apache 2.0. Stone Prover: The Stone prover is open-sourced under the Apache 2.0 license. Stwo Prover: The Stwo prover is open-sourced under the Apache 2.0 license. StarkEx Cloud Service: The StarkEx Prover cloud service is closed source, and currently operated by StarkWar. ethSTARK. Description. A library implementing ZK-STARK prover and verifier. Off-Chain Components. Prover – Open Source. Verifier – Open Source. On-Chain Components. None. StarkEx. Description. Scalability engine for commercial deployment. Off-Chain Components. Prover Service – Closed Source. Cairo Programs – Source Available. On-Chain Components. Cairo Verifier – Open Source. StarkNet / Cairo. Description. Scalability for L2 dApp developers. Off-Chain Components. Cairo Toolchain: StarkWare Toolchain License. Prover Service – Closed Source. StarkNet Prover (arriving later) – Polaris Source Available. On-Chain Components. StarkNet Polaris Verifier (arriving later) – Open Source. FAQs. What limitations does StarkWare's Source Available License impose on my use of Cairo programs? You may distribute and run Cairo programs during the lifetime of the license, but you may not make commercial use of it, nor sell it. For more details, check the terms of the license here. The Source Available License applies for a limited time, while Starkware is considering what terms will apply afterwards. Why did StarkWare adopt the Source Available License for its Cairo programs? We wish to allow scrutiny of the programs and allow the public to read and audit the code in a transparent manner, during an initial testing period. StarkWare is still considering which licenses to use in the long term when releasing various components of the Cairo toolchain and applications built on it. Why did StarkWare adopt the Source Available License for its Cairo programs? Informally, the Polaris license says that anyone may use and modify the Prover code, including for commercial use, as long as proofs generated by it are submitted to one of the white-listed Polaris Verifiers. A white-listed Verifier is a smart contract address appearing on an append-only list, which means that StarkWare may only add Verifiers to that list, but never remove them. The name Polaris (North Star) captures the essence of the license. The Polaris is a faithful address to which compasses and maps can be pointed, assisting free-roaming travellers on their myriad forays. Like the star, a Polaris Verifier is everlasting and unchanging. More coming soon. If you have any questions about our products and how to use them, talk to us:. jobs.title: Cairo-lang.org
jobs.description: Skip to content WELCOME TO CAIRO The Rust-inspired language that makes it easy to build scalable dApps with the power of validity proofs. Get started Cairo v2.12.0 WHAT IS CAIRO? Cairo lets you write provable programs without requiring a deep understanding of the underlying ZK concepts. From onchain gaming to provable ML, Cairo makes building trustless applications possible. Cairo is also the smart-contract language of Starknet, an L2 blockchain that is verified over Ethereum. About Cairo CAIRO ON STARKNET Starknet is an L2 Validity Rollup that operates on top of Ethereum, enabling dApps to massively scale without compromising on security or decentralization. Explore Layer 2 Cairo is Starknet’s smart-contract language. Cairo is purpose-built for provable computing and is a cornerstone in Starknet’s ability to scale blockchains. Open Starknet.io WHY USE CAIRO? DEVELOPER-FRIENDLY Write Rust-like code and generate proofs for program execution—math isn’t a barrier. EFFICIENT Cairo compiles down to an ad-hoc assembly, which was engineered specifically for efficient proof generation. INNOVATIVE Unshackled by EVM, Cairo is a fast-growing language that keeps delivering new and exciting features to its developers. HOW TO USE CAIRO? CODING CAIRO Learn all about Cairo both onchain and offchain Start coding PROVING CAIRO Learn all about Cairo using the blazing-fast Stwo prover to prove Cairo code Start proving HOW TO USE CAIRO? For questions or inquiries about Cairo, reach out to us on Discord or Stack Overflow. Join our Discord Ask on Stack Overflow
